audit.why: Emerald+ 51.72% over 725 games, matches the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] is stamped "Lvl 2-3" and says that on transforming, Gnar "gains a point-and-click stun chain with GNAR! (R) and Boulder Toss".
audit.why: Three errors in one sentence. GNAR! is his ultimate and cannot exist at levels 2-3. GNAR! is a directional throw, not point-and-click. And it only stuns enemies it slams into terrain — "Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned". The stun Mega Gnar actually has at those levels is Wallop (W), on a flat 7s cooldown. A player told to fear an unavailable ability will misread the real one.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Wallop and its 7s cooldown, with GNAR! placed at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hop is never given a cooldown even though the entry repeatedly builds plans around catching mini Gnar.
audit.why: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s and is mini Gnar's only escape. A 22-second rank-1 window is the single largest punish window in the matchup and the entire "catch him in mini form" plan depends on it — without the number the advice is just a mood.
audit.corrected: Hop's 22s rank-1 cooldown added to spikes[2], whys[3] and whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 3 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

audit.why: whys[0] claims Boomerang Throw outranges Tongue Lash — correct, 1100 against 900. Kept as-is.

edits.before: If Gnar transforms into Mega-Gnar, he gains a point-and-click stun chain with GNAR! (R) and Boulder Toss — the one window he can actually kill you, so save E activate for the AOE knock-up.
edits.after: If Gnar transforms into Mega-Gnar, Wallop (W) is his stun on a flat 7s cooldown — GNAR! is not his until 6 — so save Thick Skin's active for the Wallop, not for chip damage.

edits.before: From levels 4-6 the lane is a genuine skill matchup decided by transform timing. When Gnar is near full rage and close to a wall or tower, he is at his most dangerous — that is when Mega-Gnar's GNAR! (R) can pin you, Boulder Toss slows your escape, and you cannot cleanly Devour him because the AOE knock-up interrupts it. Respect that window and activate E to absorb the burst, then punish the long cooldown after. When he is locked in mini form with rage draining, he is an immobile ranged ADC — step up, land Tongue Lash to begin stacking, and make him respect that the stun-Devour combo ends his next trade attempt. Your level 6 Abyssal Voyage does not win this lane outright but does add roam threat that forces him to match or lose objectives.
edits.after: From levels 4-6 the lane is a genuine skill matchup decided by transform timing. When Gnar is near full rage and close to a wall or tower, he is at his most dangerous — that is when GNAR! can throw you into a wall for the stun, Boulder Toss slows your escape, and Wallop lands every 7s while the knockups break your Devour. Respect that window and activate E to absorb the burst, then punish the long cooldown after. When he is locked in mini form with rage draining, he is an immobile ranged ADC — step up, land Tongue Lash to begin stacking, and make him respect that the stun-Devour combo ends his next trade attempt. Your level 6 Devour does not win this lane outright, but any mini-form Gnar you catch at three stacks simply leaves the fight.

edits.before: Your Abyssal Voyage (R) comes online — Gnar's transform cooldown is a real weakness here; when he is stuck in mini form you can stack Tongue Lash freely and threaten the stun-Devour combo.
edits.after: Devour (R) comes online — mini Gnar with Hop down on its 22s rank-1 cooldown is the real target; stack to three with Tongue Lash and swallow him before his rage bar flips him to Mega.

edits.before: Mega-Gnar's rage bar is the read here: near a wall with high rage he deletes you with GNAR! into Boulder Toss; in mini form with draining rage he is an immobile target you can freely stack An Acquired Taste on.
edits.after: Mega-Gnar's rage bar is the read here: near a wall with high rage GNAR! slams you into it for the stun; in mini form with draining rage and Hop spent he is an immobile target you can freely stack An Acquired Taste on.

edits.before: Your Abyssal Voyage arrives and Gnar can no longer safely push without respecting global repositioning; when he is mini and overextended, the full Q-stun-Devour combo finally gives you a solo kill threat.
edits.after: Devour arrives and mini Gnar's only exit is Hop, down 22s at rank 1; catch him after he spends it, let Q land the third stack and swallow — a Q at 3 stuns and burns the stacks instead.

edits.before: Activate Thick Skin to shield the Mega-Gnar GNAR! knock-up and then punish with the Q stun into Devour combo
edits.after: Activate Thick Skin to shield the Wallop stun and Crunch, then punish the 7s Wallop gap by stacking to three

edits.before: Force the all-in only in Mega-Gnar form, combining Boulder Toss slow into GNAR! AOE knock-up to prevent Devour escapes
edits.after: Force the all-in only in Mega-Gnar form, combining Boulder Toss slow into a Wallop stun, saving GNAR! for a wall stun

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. W-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — Mega-only, 90s at rank 1. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: spikes[1] promised the player a level 2-3 ultimate. That is the kind of error that gets someone killed waiting for the wrong ability. The real early-Mega threat is Wallop on 7s.
